solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, number freed: 31 across to 30); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rare panic shown about China's capital

indicators.note: the panic word goes around the letter taken from China

parts.note: a panic or fright is a scare

indicators.note: the capital, or first letter, of the word China

explanation.surface: A rare scare gripping Beijing, reported in the news.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scarce is in short supply, hard to find, so uncommon.

clue.text: Just a few words will be fine

definitions.meaning: a short grammatical unit of words
a fine is a court punishment, which a judge passes

explanation.surface: Reassurance that only a few words are needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammatically a group of words; legally, the punishment a court hands down, such as a fine.

clue.text: Coming upon a river may be exciting

indicators.note: in a down clue, the coming word sits on top of the river

parts.note: an advent is an arrival or coming
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Stumbling on a river may thrill you.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the answer: something that may be exciting.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploit or escapade is by nature potentially thrilling and risky.

clue.text: Short cut that's about right

indicators.note: the word cut goes around the letter for right

parts.note: the word cut taken as written

explanation.surface: A haircut that's nearly right.
explanation.definitionFit: Brusque, abrupt speech is short in manner.

clue.text: Barrels found around ancient dumps

indicators.note: the barrels word sits around the word for ancient

parts.note: oil barrels are drums
ancient means old

explanation.surface: Old barrels lying in a rubbish tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dumps' looks like rubbish tips, but the sense is the gloomy one: 'down in the dumps' and 'in the doldrums' both mean depressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a low, listless state of spirits, as in feeling down and depressed.

clue.text: He was in a marital mix-up in a work about Edward I

definitions.text: He was in a marital mix-up

indicators.note: the work word goes around the name and the I

parts.note: an opus is a musical or literary work
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: A play about a medieval English king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edward I' looks like the king, but splits into ED and I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek king who unknowingly married his own mother, the ultimate confusion of marriage.

clue.text: Decided to be resolute

explanation.surface: Choosing to be firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Means both settled or fixed and, of a person, firmly purposeful.

clue.text: Employment of university man of learning

parts.note: a sage is a wise, learned man

explanation.surface: A university hiring a scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: The way something is employed or put to use.

clue.text: Fast river traps journalist

indicators.note: the river word holds the journalist inside it

parts.note: the Spey is a Scottish river
ED abbreviates editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A rushing river catches a reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick, rapid, swift in motion.

clue.text: Aerial I'd put back on a post

indicators.note: put back signals the letters of I'd are turned around

parts.note: the letters of I'd without the apostrophe
a pole is a post

explanation.surface: Fixing a radio aerial onto a post.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple radio antenna made of two rods, a common type of aerial.

clue.text: Don't let it bother you that you've always been inattentive

definitions.meaning: a reassuring phrase telling someone to forget about a matter
read literally, never having paid any mind, never attending

explanation.surface: Reassurance to someone who has never paid attention.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom dismisses a worry; read word by word it says no attention has ever been paid.

clue.text: Business deal

definitions.meaning: commerce, a line of work such as the building business
to buy and sell, to traffic in goods

explanation.surface: A business deal.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is commerce or an occupation; the verb sense is to buy and sell goods.

clue.text: Long times in the onslaught

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words 'the onslaught', spanning the join

explanation.surface: An attack that seems to go on for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: An aeon is an immeasurably long period, so the plural means ages.

clue.text: Police chief is a snake in the grass

parts.note: a copper is a police officer
a chief is the head of an organisation

explanation.surface: The head of the police force turns out to be a traitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snake in the grass' reads as a traitor, but here it is literal: a venomous American viper.
explanation.definitionFit: The copperhead is a venomous pit viper of North America, literally a serpent lurking in grass.

clue.text: Exclusive treatment for a political offence

definitions.text: Exclusive treatment for a political offence

parts.words: Exclusive treatment for a political offence
parts.note: exclusive here means shutting out: the punishment of exile from one's country

explanation.surface: Special VIP treatment for a political crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exclusive' suggests privileged, but here it means excluding.
explanation.definitionFit: Exile from one's country, a traditional punishment for dissidents.

clue.text: Bottle company prompt coming about midday

indicators.note: the urge word goes around the letter from the middle of day

parts.note: to prompt someone is to urge them
the middle letter of the word day

explanation.surface: A firm encouraging someone around noon to have a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' is British slang for nerve or courage, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, having bottle means having nerve, pluck and bravery.

clue.text: Their losses may get roundabout compensation

definitions.text: Their losses may get roundabout compensation

parts.words: Their losses may get roundabout compensation
parts.note: plays on the saying that what you lose on these playground rides you gain on the roundabouts

explanation.surface: Losses recovered by an indirect route of compensation.
explanation.walkthrough: The British saying 'what you lose on the swings you gain on the roundabouts' means losses in one area are offset elsewhere; a roundabout is a merry-go-round.
explanation.definitionFit: Playground seats hung on chains, partnered in the proverb with roundabouts that make good the losses.

clue.text: At one time he fought in spectacles

definitions.text: At one time he fought in spectacles

parts.words: At one time he fought in spectacles
parts.note: spectacles here are public shows in a Roman arena, not glasses

explanation.surface: A man who once boxed wearing his glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spectacles' suggests eyewear; the spectacles are arena shows of ancient Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman combatant who fought in public shows held in the arena.

clue.text: Restrict dangerous driver — he's often flat out on the road

definitions.text: he's often flat out on the road

parts.note: to hedge in is to restrict
a road hog is a reckless driver

explanation.surface: Curbing a reckless motorist who drives flat out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat out' suggests full speed, but it means run over, lying dead on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiny mammal often sadly found squashed on roads as roadkill.

clue.text: Girl entertaining relatives needs capital

indicators.note: the girl's name holds the relatives word inside, as a host entertains guests

parts.note: Peg is a girl's name, short for Margaret
one's kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: A girl hosting her family needs money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests money; it is the old name for Beijing, China's capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the older romanised name of Beijing, China's chief city.

clue.text: Firing range

definitions.meaning: the distance a bullet carries, as in within earshot of a shot

explanation.surface: A place for shooting practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Means the act of firing a gun and the reach of its bullet.

clue.text: Leave scribbled note offering lift

indicators.note: scribbled suggests letters dashed off untidily, so the word leave is rearranged

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a hasty note offering a ride.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something up is to give it a lift upward.

clue.text: Sallies follow a direction to arms

indicators.note: the witty remarks come after the compass letter

parts.note: E is east, a compass direction
sallies are witty remarks, quips

explanation.surface: Troops sally forth following orders to take up arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sallies' looks military, but means witty remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: To arm someone is to supply or fit them out with gear.

clue.text: Write poems to the Salvation Army in Ukraine

definitions.note: the definition describes a place found in that country, a port

parts.note: odes are poems

explanation.surface: Writing verse for a charity working in Ukraine.
explanation.definitionFit: A major Black Sea port city located in the country named.

clue.text: Light and delicate piano had us quite excited

indicators.note: letters that are excited are stirred up, so the words piano had us are rearranged

explanation.surface: A light, delicate piece of music that thrilled the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes fabric so fine and sheer it is almost transparent, filmy and gauzy.

clue.text: Make sense of a clergyman at university

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, a clergyman's degree
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A vicar at college working out a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures or facts that add up are consistent and credible.

clue.text: Its mating call comes from the other side

definitions.text: Its mating call comes from the other side

parts.words: Its mating call comes from the other side
parts.note: in chess, checkmate against this piece is announced by the opponent across the board

explanation.surface: Sounds like an animal's mating cry heard from across the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mating call' suggests birds, but the mating is checkmate, called by the player on the other side of the board.
explanation.definitionFit: The chess piece whose checkmate ends the game, announced by the opposing player.

clue.text: Classical maid who always had the last word

definitions.text: Classical maid who always had the last word

parts.words: Classical maid who always had the last word
parts.note: the Greek nymph cursed to repeat only the final words of others

explanation.surface: An argumentative girl from antiquity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last word' suggests winning arguments, but she could only repeat others' final words.
explanation.definitionFit: The nymph of Greek myth condemned to repeat the closing words of others' speech.

clue.text: Try to walk like a crab and slide about

definitions.text: Try to walk like a crab

indicators.note: about signals the word slide is turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone imitating a crab's walk and slipping around.
explanation.definitionFit: To move sideways furtively, much as a crab scuttles sideways.

clue.text: Game that's bound to go with whisky

parts.note: a bound is a leap or hop
Scotch is whisky from Scotland

explanation.surface: A game that is obliged to come with a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' reads as obliged, but it is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's playground game of hopping through squares chalked on the ground.

clue.text: A quiet little craving for food

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
petite means small or little

explanation.surface: A slight, quiet hunger.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunger or desire to eat is the core meaning of the word.

clue.text: Despicable person possibly got time inside

indicators.note: the period word goes inside the rearranged letters
possibly signals a possible rearrangement of the word got

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A villain who probably got jail time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals the anagram and 'inside' the insertion. The answer is British slang for a worthless scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang term of contempt for a low, worthless rogue.
